newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT - RUGBY UNION - Wallabies just a warm-up, says Dowd.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - RUGBY UNION - Wallabies just a warm-up, says Dowd.

text.p: WELLINGTON, July 7 - The Springbok front row will be a much tougher proposition for the All Blacks on July 19 than the Wallabies were in their rugby test on Saturday in Christchurch, according to New Zealand prop Craig Dowd.
New Zealand won Saturday's Bledisloe Cup rugby match 30-13 because the tight five grabbed such an immediate scrum advantage that the Australians could not compete.
All three New Zealand front rowers were relieved afterwards, because until then they had been unable to generate the power this year they had in previous big games.
Dowd said the improvement was due to the motivational challenge of playing better opposition -- and the South Africans presented the ultimate challenge at Ellis Park in Johannesburg.
"They (the Boks) will be a hell of a lot better than the Wallabies," he said.
Both Dowd and fellow prop Olo Brown said the All Black tight five could scrum better than they did on Saturday.

"I suppose it's the intensity of the game you're playing. It's easy to slacken off and give the ball to the backs against teams like Argentina, but games against teams like Australia and South Africa are those that really test us.
"The Boks' forwards are a very good unit. They base their game around their scrum. It's the physical thing again -- the South African mentality. They base everything on strength and size."
